title: kactivitymanagerd pegs a CPU core at 100% when many files are added to the recently used list (recently-used.xbel) sequentially
line: kactivitymanagerd no longer keeps a CPU core busy while many files are added to the recent files list one after another.
explanation: Every time recently-used.xbel changed, the RecentlyUsedEventSpy plugin re-read the whole file and ran KApplicationTrader::query (a scan of all installed applications) for every application entry of every bookmark, although it only registers the bookmarks accessed since its last run. With about 1000 bookmarks that took close to a second per change, so a stream of saves or downloads kept a core busy. The change does the application lookup only for bookmarks accessed since the last run, using the same test as the loop that registers them.

commits.message:
RecentlyUsedEventSpy: only look up applications of new bookmarks

Each time recently-used.xbel changed, the plugin looked up the
application of every bookmark in it, although only new bookmarks are
used. Adding many files in a row kept a core busy; skip the old ones.

BUG: 470026

media.caption: Master: top on kactivitymanagerd while a 1000-entry recently-used.xbel gets a new file every 0.5 s: 84.6% CPU.
With the fix, same flood: 3.5% CPU.

review.text: Clean, minimal fix targeting the exact CPU hotspot in RecentlyUsedEventSpyPlugin::fileUpdated(): skipping KApplicationTrader::query for bookmarks not accessed since m_lastUpdate avoids rescanning installed applications for every historical entry on each recently-used.xbel write. Reusing the same accessedSinceLastRun predicate for both parsing and registration guarantees consistency, and verification shows CPU usage dropping from ~85% to ~3.5% while actually improving recording accuracy under load. The unrelated QReadWriteLock/SQL activity loop mentioned in later bug comments is transparently noted as separate.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix targeting the exact CPU hotspot in RecentlyUsedEventSpyPlugin::fileUpdated(): skipping KApplicationTrader::query for bookmarks not accessed since m_lastUpdate avoids rescanning installed applications for every historical entry on each recently-used.xbel write. Reusing the same accessedSinceLastRun predicate for both parsing and registration guarantees consistency, and verification shows CPU usage dropping from ~85% to ~3.5% while actually improving recording accuracy under load. The unrelated QReadWriteLock/SQL activity loop mentioned in later bug comments is transparently noted as separate.

The cost is exactly where the report and perf point: fileUpdated() ran KApplicationTrader::query for every bookmark:application of the whole xbel on each change, while only bookmarks newer than m_lastUpdate are ever used. Since the <bookmark> start element sets added/modified/visited before its application children are parsed, gating the lookup with the same predicate as the registration loop is correct and old bookmarks never reach latestApplication(). Rig numbers (~85% to ~4% of a core under a 0.5 s flood) and the functional check (all 8 new files recorded with the right apps, vs 3/8 on master) support it, and the commit text matches the diff. MartinG's DBus/DeleteData loop from the duplicate 484837 (c9-c17) is a separate cause that does not match this report's title and is better split into its own bug than held against this fix.
